PM

Also Building Toward: Product Management

I build things end-to-end, and that's exactly why Product Management pulls at me. On MediAI, my job didn't start with a model — it started with a question: what's actually broken for a patient who can't get to a doctor? India has 1 doctor per 1,456 people, prescriptions nobody explains, and no easy way to know who's available nearby. Only after that problem was mapped clearly did the Random Forest model, the doctor finder, and the prescription analyzer make sense as solutions — not the other way around.

That habit — sit with the problem before reaching for the tool — is the same one I've practiced through the JECRC Incubation Centre and NITI Aayog's Mentor India program, both built around turning ambiguous, real-world gaps into structured, buildable ideas.

What I'd bring to a PM role isn't a pitch deck version of empathy — it's the fact that I've sat on the engineering side of the table. I know what a vague requirement costs a dev team, because I've been the dev team. I want to spend my career on the side of the table that decides what gets built and why — grounded in the same research-first instinct that got MediAI to 94% accuracy instead of a guess.
